items.stem:
Study the production possibilities of an economy:
Combination | A | B | C | D | E | F
Cement (units) | 0 | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 | 25
Steel (units) | 185 | 170 | 140 | 100 | 55 | 0
(i) Calculate the MOC of moving from B to C.
(ii) Is the MOC rising, constant or falling? What does this tell you about the shape of the PPF?
(iii) Can the economy produce 15 units of cement and 105 units of steel? Why?
(iv) How would the PPF change if a new technology raises the output of both goods?
items.answer: (i) 30/5 = 6; (ii) Rising; the PPF is concave to the origin; (iii) No: at 15 units of cement the maximum is 100 units of steel; the point lies outside the PPF; (iv) It shifts outward (to the right)

Computers (units) | 25 | 24 | 20 | 12 | 0

items.answer: (i) 1, 4, 8, 12 units of computers per unit of cars; (ii) Concave to the origin: MOC rises because resources are not equally efficient in both goods; (iii) It is inside the PPF (maximum computers at 1 cars is 24): resources are under-utilised; (iv) The PPF shifts inward (to the left)
